gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies that the cutoff is not one near the PML endpoints, so the nearest reflected kernel remains in the remainder on the full boundary product and the required exponential operator estimate is unsupported. Its stated repair requires chi_im=1 near both corners, directly matching the gold repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The endpoint-excluding cutoff fails to localize the nearest reflected boundary interaction; consequently the separated remainder is not shown to be exponentially small in the operator estimate needed for the Neumann-series arguments.

component_coverage.gold_component: The PML cutoff excludes the outer endpoints, leaving the nearest reflected boundary-boundary kernel in the remainder and invalidating the required all-boundary exponential estimate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly locates the failure at corners/endpoints, explains the surviving nearest-image singular kernel and loss of exponential smallness, identifies the unsupported Neumann-series input, and supplies the endpoint cutoff correction.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies that the field is defined or controlled only in the physical domain while the theorem claims convergence for compact sets in the full truncated domain, including the PML. It explains why the PML comparison is unavailable or false and gives the matching restriction to compact subsets of the physical domain.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The computable-field estimate is overclaimed on compact sets meeting the PML because the exact convergence estimate and physical-field comparison apply only on compact subsets of the physical domain.

component_coverage.gold_component: The theorem claims a compact-set field estimate throughout Omega_R although the supporting PDE estimate and comparison are established only for K compactly contained in Omega_p; the repair is to restrict K to Omega_p.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction directly states the physical-domain scope of the exact theorem, explains the failure of convergence claims for compact sets meeting the PML, and supplies the same domain restriction as repair.
